events.title: Iraq war decision later condemned by Chilcot inquiry for process and planning failures
events.summary: Blair’s government joined the US-led invasion of Iraq in March 2003. Consequence: The war produced prolonged conflict and instability; the 2016 Iraq Inquiry found that peaceful options had not been exhausted, intelligence judgments were presented with unjustified certainty, and post-war planning was inadequate.

events.court_outcome: After a 16-month investigation, prosecutors announced that no charges would be brought.
events.migration_context: No migration connection required.
events.public_controversy: The scandal badly damaged trust and overshadowed Blair’s final months, but the criminal investigation did not establish an offence.

events.relationship: Occurred during term

sources.label: Guardian — Blairmore fund exposed in Panama Papers

events.court_outcome: The existence of the offshore investment and Cameron’s prior stake were confirmed. The reporting did not establish that Cameron broke tax law by owning the shares.
events.migration_context: No migration connection required.
events.public_controversy: The controversy centred on transparency and the contrast between Cameron’s public stance on tax avoidance and his family’s offshore arrangements.
events.politician_response: Cameron said the investment had been properly taxed and that he sold the stake before entering Downing Street. His statements evolved over several days before he gave the fuller disclosure.

events.title: Woman jailed for killing man while he sexually assaulted her loses sentence appeal

events.relationship: Underlying killing occurred during Theresa May’s term; later appeal occurred under Keir Starmer.

events.title: Henry Nowak stabbed to death, then handcuffed by police while dying
events.summary: Eighteen-year-old Henry Nowak was fatally stabbed by Vickrum Singh Digwa. Digwa told police that Nowak had racially attacked him; officers handcuffed the wounded Nowak and appeared to dismiss his statements that he had been stabbed. A court later found Digwa had lied about being the victim of racism. Bodycam footage triggered protests and a major policing controversy.
events.evidence: AP court and bodycam reporting; police-watchdog follow-up
events.relationship: Murder occurred during Keir Starmer’s term; sentencing, protests and misconduct investigation continued in 2026.

sources.label: AP — court outcome, bodycam and protest

events.case_status: murder closed / police conduct investigation open
events.court_outcome: Digwa was convicted of murder and sentenced to life with a minimum term of 21 years.
events.migration_context: The killer was identified in AP reporting as Sikh; the reliable sources cited here do not establish that the murder was caused by immigration policy.
events.public_controversy: The court rejected Digwa’s claim that he had been the victim of racist aggression. Public debate focused on whether the accusation of racism distorted police decision-making; Nowak’s father urged that the case not be used to inflame racial or religious division.

events.title: Starmer resists new national grooming-gangs inquiry, then accepts one after Casey review

events.title: Starmer government cuts winter fuel support for most pensioners, then restores it to millions
events.summary: Soon after taking office, Labour restricted winter fuel payments to the poorest pensioners as part of its fiscal tightening. Consequence: The decision affected roughly 11 million pensioners, generated months of backlash and was widely blamed for damaging Labour politically.
events.evidence: Reuters — winter fuel payments restored to millions
events.relationship: Occurred during term

sources.label: Reuters — winter fuel payments restored to millions

events.court_outcome: The government retained some means-testing, so this was a substantial reversal rather than a complete restoration of the old universal system.
events.migration_context: No migration connection required.
events.politician_response: Starmer and Reeves defended the initial cut as necessary because of the public finances, then later said improved finances allowed support to be widened again.
events.decision_made: Soon after taking office, Labour restricted winter fuel payments to the poorest pensioners as part of its fiscal tightening.
events.consequence: The decision affected roughly 11 million pensioners, generated months of backlash and was widely blamed for damaging Labour politically.

events.reversal_or_admission: In June 2025 the government restored payments to millions of pensioners, a major U-turn costing about £1.25 billion.
